questions.question: Which of the following is a compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Water (H₂O)** is a compound because it is formed by the chemical combination of two elements, hydrogen and oxygen, in a fixed ratio of 2:1.
 
• It has distinct chemical properties different from the properties of its constituent elements (hydrogen and oxygen).
 
• Water is a pure substance that cannot be separated into its elements by physical means but can be broken down into hydrogen and oxygen through electrolysis.
 
• It is essential for life on Earth, forming a major part of biological systems and being involved in various physical and chemical processes.
 
• As a compound, water exhibits unique properties like high boiling and melting points, surface tension, and its ability to dissolve numerous substances, making it a universal solvent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxygen (O₂):**

 
 
• Oxygen is an element and exists as a diatomic molecule (O₂) in its most stable form.
 
• It is a colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas essential for respiration in living organisms and combustion reactions.
 
• Oxygen forms compounds with nearly all other elements and is a major component of the Earth's atmosphere (approximately 21%).
 
 
 
• **Iron (Fe):**
 
 
• Iron is a metallic element and is one of the most abundant elements on Earth.
 
• It is widely used in construction, manufacturing, and making alloys like steel.
 
• Iron is also essential for biological processes, as it is a key component of hemoglobin in blood, which transports oxygen throughout the body.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur (S):**
 
 
• Sulphur is a non-metallic element commonly found in nature in its elemental form or as part of various compounds like sulfates and sulfides.
 
• It has diverse applications, including the production of sulfuric acid, fertilizers, and rubber vulcanization.
 
• Sulphur is essential for life as it forms part of amino acids like cysteine and methionine.
 
 
 
• **Compounds:**
 
 
• Compounds are substances formed when two or more elements chemically combine in a fixed proportion.
 
• They have properties distinct from their constituent elements.
 
• Examples include water (H₂O), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and sodium chloride (NaCl).

questions.question: What is self-induction?

options.text: Induction of EMF in one coil due to a current in a nearby coil
Induction of EMF in a coil due to motion in a magnetic field
Induction of EMF in a coil due to a change in its own current
Generation of current in a coil due to temperature changes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Induction of EMF in a coil due to a change in its own current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Self-induction** is the phenomenon in which an electromotive force (EMF) is induced in a coil due to a change in the current flowing through the same coil.
 
• The induced EMF opposes the change in current, as per **Lenz's Law**, and is mathematically expressed as **E = -L (dI/dt)**, where L is the self-inductance of the coil.
 
• Self-inductance is a property of a coil that depends on its dimensions, number of turns, and the medium surrounding it. It is measured in **henry (H)**.
 
• Self-induction plays a critical role in devices like **transformers, inductors, and electrical circuits** where controlling or opposing rapid changes in current is essential.
 
• It is an important principle in electromagnetic theory and is widely applied in technologies like AC systems and communication devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**

 
 
• Electromagnetic induction is the process of inducing an EMF or current in a conductor due to the relative motion between the conductor and a magnetic field or due to changes in the magnetic flux.
 
• The concept of self-induction is a specific case of electromagnetic induction where the coil induces EMF in itself rather than in another coil.
 
• These principles are fundamental to modern electrical engineering and power systems.

questions.question: Which law explains the colours of black bodies including the Sun and other stars in terms of their temperatures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wien's Displacement Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wien's Displacement Law** explains the relationship between the temperature of a black body and the wavelength at which it emits radiation most strongly.
 
• It states that the wavelength corresponding to the peak emission of radiation is inversely proportional to the temperature of the black body. **Mathematically, λ_max = b/T**, where **λ_max** is the peak wavelength, **T** is the temperature, and **b** is Wien's constant (approximately **2.897 × 10⁻³ m·K**).
 
• This law helps us understand the colors emitted by black bodies like stars, including the **Sun**, based on their surface temperature. For example, hotter stars emit blue light, while cooler stars emit red light.
 
• The law was formulated by **Wilhelm Wien** in **1893** and is a fundamental concept in **thermodynamics and astrophysics**.
 
• It is widely applied in determining the temperature of celestial objects by analyzing the spectrum of their emitted radiation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hooke's Law:**

 
 
• Hooke's Law pertains to the **elasticity of materials** and states that the force needed to extend or compress a spring is proportional to the distance it is stretched or compressed (**F = kx**, where **k** is the spring constant).
 
• It is unrelated to black body radiation or temperature.
 
 
 
• **Snell's Law:**
 
 
• Snell's Law describes the **refraction of light** as it passes from one medium to another, stating that the ratio of the sine of the angles of incidence and refraction is proportional to the refractive indices of the media (**n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂**).
 
• This law is used in optics and is not related to the emission of radiation by black bodies.
 
 
 
• **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion:**
 
 
• These laws describe the motion of planets around the Sun:
 
• **1st Law:** Planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus.
 
• **2nd Law:** A line segment joining a planet and the Sun sweeps out equal areas during equal intervals of time.
 
• **3rd Law:** The square of the orbital period of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
 
• While these laws are significant in celestial mechanics, they do not explain the colors of black bodies based on their temperature.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• **Wien's Displacement Law** is essential for understanding the spectrum of stars and other celestial objects, allowing scientists to estimate their **surface temperatures**.
 
• The Sun, for example, emits radiation most strongly at a wavelength of approximately **500 nm** (green light), corresponding to its surface temperature of about **5778 K**.
 
• It is a crucial tool in **astrophysics** and helps in the study of **stellar evolution**.

questions.question: Which metals are generally used for electrical transmission lines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper and aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Copper** is widely used in electrical transmission lines due to its excellent conductivity, durability, and resistance to corrosion.
 
• **Aluminium** is commonly used because it is lightweight, cost-effective, and has a high conductivity-to-weight ratio.
 
• Both metals are preferred in applications requiring efficient power transmission over long distances. 
 
• Aluminium is often used in high-voltage transmission lines, while copper is preferred for lower-voltage applications and in areas where space is limited. 
 
• Modern transmission cables often use **aluminium core reinforced with steel** (ACSR) to improve strength while maintaining conductivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrical Conductivity:**

 
 
• Copper has one of the highest electrical conductivity values among metals, second only to silver.
 
• Aluminium's conductivity is lower than copper but is still highly efficient for transmission purposes.
 
 
 
• **Cost Considerations:**
 
 
• Aluminium is significantly cheaper than copper, making it an economical choice for large-scale transmission projects.
 
• Copper, while more expensive, is used where higher performance and durability are required.
 
 
 
• **Strength and Weight:**
 
 
• Aluminium's lower density makes it lighter and easier to install in overhead transmission lines.
 
• Steel reinforcement in aluminium cables increases tensile strength for long-distance applications.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Copper vs Aluminium:**
 
 
• Copper is used in underground cables, electrical wiring, and machinery due to its compact nature and reliability.
 
• Aluminium is used in overhead lines, including long-distance power transmission and distribution networks.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Aspect:**
 
 
• Both copper and aluminium are recyclable and contribute to sustainable energy systems.
 
• Efficient transmission reduces energy loss, making them critical for modern energy-efficient grids.

• **Other Household Uses:** Baking soda is widely used for cleaning, deodorizing, and personal care, such as teeth whitening and skin exfoliation.

questions.question: DNA polymerase catalyses the addition of nucleotides during DNA replication. Its main role is to:

options.text: Synthesise new DNA strands complementary to the template
Remove RNA primers from the lagging strand

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Synthesise new DNA strands complementary to the template**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DNA polymerase** is a key enzyme involved in the process of **DNA replication**.
 
• Its primary function is to **catalyse the addition of nucleotides** to the growing DNA strand, ensuring it is **complementary** to the original template strand.
 
• The enzyme works in the **5’ to 3’ direction**, adding new nucleotides to the **free 3’-OH group** of the preceding nucleotide.
 
• DNA polymerase requires a **template strand** and a **primer** to initiate synthesis.
 
• This enzyme plays a critical role in maintaining the **accuracy and fidelity** of DNA replication by performing **proofreading** and correcting errors.
 
• DNA polymerase is essential for **cell division** as it ensures that genetic information is accurately passed to daughter cells.
 
• Replication of DNA is crucial for processes such as **growth, repair, and reproduction** in living organisms.
 
• There are different types of DNA polymerase enzymes, including **DNA polymerase I, II, and III** in prokaryotes and **DNA polymerase alpha, beta, delta, and epsilon** in eukaryotes, each specialized for different functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ligate Okazaki fragments together**__

 __
 
• This function is performed by the enzyme **DNA ligase**, not DNA polymerase.
 
• Okazaki fragments are short DNA sequences synthesized on the **lagging strand** during replication.
 
• DNA ligase joins these fragments by forming **phosphodiester bonds** between adjacent nucleotides.
 
 
 
• **Unwind the DNA double helix**__
 __
 
• This process is carried out by the enzyme **helicase**, not DNA polymerase.
 
• Helicase breaks the hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs, allowing the two strands of DNA to separate and serve as templates.
 
 
 
• **Remove RNA primers from the lagging strand**__
 
 
• The removal of RNA primers is performed by enzymes such as **DNA polymerase I** in prokaryotes and **RNase H** in eukaryotes.
 
• DNA polymerase I also replaces the RNA primers with DNA nucleotides after their removal.

questions.question: In a laboratory thermometer, what is the usual temperature range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-10 °C to 110 °C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The usual temperature range of a laboratory thermometer is **-10 °C to 110 °C**, suitable for various experimental purposes.
 
• Laboratory thermometers are primarily used to measure temperature in **scientific research and experiments**.
 
• These thermometers are **non-clinical** and are not meant for measuring body temperature.
 
• The thermometer typically uses **mercury or alcohol** as the thermometric liquid due to their high sensitivity to temperature changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermometer Types:**

 
 
• **Clinical Thermometers:** Used to measure human body temperature, typically ranging from 35 °C to 42 °C.
 
• **Laboratory Thermometers:** Designed for experiments, with a broader range of -10 °C to 110 °C.
 
• **Digital Thermometers:** Use electronic sensors for temperature measurement, offering higher accuracy.
 
 
 
• **Thermometric Liquids:**
 
 
• **Mercury:** High thermal expansion and accuracy; used in traditional thermometers.
 
• **Alcohol:** Colored alcohol is used for better visibility and low freezing points.
 
 
 
• **Working Principle:** Laboratory thermometers operate on the principle of **thermal expansion**, where the liquid expands or contracts with temperature changes.
 
• **Precautions:**
 
 
• Ensure the thermometer is upright while taking measurements.
 
• Avoid measuring temperatures beyond the thermometer's range to prevent damage.
 
• Handle mercury thermometers carefully due to mercury's toxicity.

__**Explanation-**__

**Echinoderms**, a group that includes sea stars (starfish), sea cucumbers, sea urchins, sand dollars, and brittle stars, possess a unique structural feature known as the water vascular system.

The water vascular system is a network of water-filled canals that function in locomotion, feeding, gas exchange, and sensory perception. Here's how it generally works:

__
 
• **Water Inflow:** Seawater enters the system through a sieve-like structure on the echinoderm's body surface called the** madreporite.**
 
• **Stone Canal:** From the madreporite, water then flows into a short canal, often lined with calcareous material, known as the stone canal.
 
• **Ring Canal**: The stone canal leads to a circular canal, the ring canal, that surrounds the esophagus.
 
• **Radial Canal(s):** Connected to the ring canal are five (or multiples of five) radial canals. These extend into each of the echinoderm's arms (if arms are present).
 
• **Tube Feet:** Off of the radial canals are many lateral canals, each terminating in a muscular, often sucker-tipped, extension known as a tube foot or podium. The sequential contraction and expansion of the tube feet, controlled by the water pressure within the canals, assist with locomotion, enable feeding, and facilitate gas exchange.

The water vascular system in echinoderms allows these marine animals to move effectively despite having no centralized brain nor discernable front or back to their bodies.

**Conclusion-**__ Water vascular system is observed in Echinoderms.

questions.question: One of the roots of the equation x² − 4x + k = 0 is x = 3. The other root is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In any **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0, the **Sum of Roots** is given by the formula −b/a.

For the equation x² − 4x + k = 0, the coefficients are a = 1 and b = −4.

**Sum of roots** = −(−4)/1 = 4.

Since one root is 3, let the other root be x. Then, 3 + x = 4.

Solving for x: x = 4 − 3 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is x = 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The equation is x² − 4x + k = 0 and one **root** is x = 3.

**Formula Used:** Substitution method and **Quadratic Factorization**.

⇒ Substituting x = 3 into the equation: 3² − 4(3) + k = 0

⇒ 9 − 12 + k = 0

⇒ −3 + k = 0

⇒ k = 3

⇒ The complete equation is x² − 4x + 3 = 0

⇒ x² − 3x − x + 3 = 0

⇒ x(x − 3) − 1(x − 3) = 0

⇒ (x − 3)(x − 1) = 0

⇒ x = 3 or x = 1

**∴ The correct answer is x = 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Product of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the **Product of Roots** (αβ) is equal to c/a.

Discriminant and Nature of Roots

The **Discriminant** D = b² − 4ac determines the nature: if D > 0 roots are real and distinct; if D = 0 roots are real and equal; if D < 0 roots are imaginary.

Vieta's Formulas

These formulas relate the **coefficients** of a polynomial to sums and products of its roots, helping solve for unknown variables like k.</p

Given (a² + b²) ÷ 2ab = 3. Dividing numerator and denominator by ab, we get: (a/b + b/a) ÷ 2 = 3 ⇒ **a/b + b/a = 6**.

Let a/b = x, then x + 1/x = 6. Solving for the **larger root**, x = 3 + 2√2.

The required ratio is a : (a + b), which is equivalent to x : (x + 1).

Ratio = (3 + 2√2) : (4 + 2√2). Multiplying both terms by (√2 − 1) gives (√2 + 1) : 2√2.

⇒ (a² + b² + 2ab) / (a² + b² − 2ab) = (3 + 1) / (3 − 1)

⇒ (a + b)² / (a − b)² = 4 / 2 = 2

⇒ (a + b) / (a − b) = √2

⇒ a + b = √2a − √2b

⇒ b(1 + √2) = a(√2 − 1)

⇒ a/b = (√2 + 1) / (√2 − 1)

Rationalizing the denominator for a/b:

⇒ a/b = [(√2 + 1)(√2 + 1)] / [(√2 − 1)(√2 + 1)] = (2 + 1 + 2√2) / (2 − 1) = 3 + 2√2

Calculating the ratio a : (a + b):

⇒ a / (a + b) = (3 + 2√2) / (4 + 2√2)

To simplify, multiply numerator and denominator by (√2 − 1):

⇒ Num = (3 + 2√2)(√2 − 1) = 3√2 − 3 + 4 − 2√2 = √2 + 1

⇒ Denom = (4 + 2√2)(√2 − 1) = 4√2 − 4 + 4 − 2√2 = 2√2

⇒ Ratio = (√2 + 1) / 2√2

**∴ The correct answer is (√2 + 1) : 2√2.**

Quadratic Formula

To rationalize a denominator like (x + √y), multiply both numerator and denominator by its conjugate (x − √y) to eliminate the radical term from the denominator.</p

questions.question: A cricketer was averaging 49 runs after 9 innings. How many runs does she need to score in her 10th innings the take the average to 52?

Increase in **average** = 52 − 49 = 3 runs.

Total increase needed for 9 previous **innings** = 9 × 3 = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9b6e2bf6f664b7bbca56b5381ab932e32ffd1d61099d8608c913eef9a9a633e.png]

Total runs = Average × Number of innings

⇒ Total runs after **9 innings** = 9 × 49 = 441

⇒ Total runs after **10 innings** = 10 × 52 = 520

⇒ Runs needed in **10th innings** = Total runs (10 innings) − Total runs (9 innings)

⇒ Runs needed = 520 − 441 = 79

Arithmetic Average

The average of a set of observations is the sum of the observations divided by the number of observations (Average = Sum ÷ n).

Change in Average

When a new value is added to a group, the new value = New Average + [Previous Count × (New Average − Old Average)].

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups is given by (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: If x + (1)/(x) = 3 then find the value of x¹² + (1)/(x ¹²⁾ ?

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2 and x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k.

Given x + 1/x = 3 ⇒ x² + 1/x² = 3² − 2 = 7.

Then x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 7² − 2 = 47.

Finally, x¹² + 1/x¹² = (x⁴)³ + 1/(x⁴)³ = 47³ − 3(47) = 103823 − 141 = 103682.

**∴ The correct answer is 103682.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x + 1/x = 3

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c8b60572751c9d3f94603e09d62ac3cff690376214bcbfde638a9effeef00b7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x + 1/x = 3

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 3² ⇒ x² + 1/x² + 2 = 9

⇒ x² + 1/x² = 7

⇒ (x² + 1/x²)² = 7² ⇒ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ + 2 = 49

⇒ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 47

⇒ (x⁴ + 1/x⁴)³ = 47³

⇒ (x⁴)³ + (1/x⁴)³ + 3(x⁴)(1/x⁴)(x⁴ + 1/x⁴) = 103823

⇒ x¹² + 1/x¹² + 3(47) = 103823

⇒ x¹² + 1/x¹² = 103823 − 141

⇒ x¹² + 1/x¹² = 103682

**∴ The correct answer is 103682.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Identity

If the value of x + 1/x = k, then the value of x² + 1/x² is always equal to k² − 2.

Cube Identity

If the value of x + 1/x = k, then the value of x³ + 1/x³ is always equal to k³ − 3k.

Difference Identity

If the value of x − 1/x = k, then the value of x² + 1/x² is equal to k² + 2.</p

questions.question: The average speed of the car is 16 km/hr during the whole journey. If the first half of the journey is covered at 40 km/hr, then find the speed with which the car covers the second half of the journey. (in km/hr)

questions.question: The number of diagonals in a pentadecagon is:

Number of diagonals in a polygon with **n sides** = n(n − 3) ÷ 2

For a **pentadecagon**, the number of sides **n = 15**.

Substituting n = 15 in the formula:

Diagonals = 15 × (15 − 3) ÷ 2 = 15 × 12 ÷ 2

Diagonals = 15 × 6 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

⇒ Out of these lines, n lines are the sides of the polygon.

⇒ Diagonals = Total lines − Number of sides

⇒ Diagonals = [n(n − 1) ÷ 2] − n

⇒ Diagonals = [15 × 14 ÷ 2] − 15

Regular Polygon Angles

questions.question: A water pump can fill a tank in 2 hours. Because of a leak in the tank it takes 4 hours to fill the tank. If the tank is full, how much time will the leak take to empty it ?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in x hours and together with a leak it takes y hours to fill, the time taken by the leak to empty the full tank is (x × y) ÷ (y − x) hours.

Here, x = 2 hours and y = 4 hours.

Time taken by leak = (2 × 4) ÷ (4 − 2)

⇒ Time taken = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by water pump alone to fill the tank = 2 hours.

Time taken by water pump and leak together to fill the tank = 4 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual times taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Pipes / Leak**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Pump

 4 ÷ 2 = 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined Efficiency = Efficiency of Pump + Efficiency of Leak

⇒ 1 = 2 + Efficiency of Leak

⇒ Efficiency of Leak = 1 − 2 = −1 unit/hour

The negative sign indicates that the leak is emptying the tank.

⇒ Time taken by the leak to empty the tank = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Leak

⇒ Time taken = 4 ÷ 1 = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

questions.question: The mean of 5 numbers is 17. If one number is excluded their mean is 15. Find the square of an excluded number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Excluded value = Old Average + (New Count × Drop in Average)

Excluded value = 17 + (4 × (17 − 15)) = 17 + (4 × 2) = 25

Square of the excluded value = 25² = 625

**∴ The correct answer is 625.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean of 5 numbers = 17

Mean of 4 numbers (after excluding one) = 15

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

Excluded number = (Sum of 5 numbers) − (Sum of 4 numbers)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4bac68a90af62c84fb5445e3e7eb3a5d1f43a1830d693f216e2f803a4831508.png] 

⇒ Total sum of 5 numbers = 5 × 17 = 85

⇒ Total sum of 4 numbers = 4 × 15 = 60

⇒ Excluded number = 85 − 60 = 25

⇒ Square of the number = 25 × 25 = 625

**∴ The correct answer is 625.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average (Mean)

Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Effect of Excluding a Number

If the excluded number is greater than the original average, the new average will decrease. If it is smaller, the average will increase.

Weighted Average

When two groups with different averages are combined: New Average = (n₁×A₁ + n₂×A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The ratio of new expenditure to that of the initial expenditure is 15 : 16. If the price of petrol is increased by 25% then the consumption of petrol is decreased by x%. Find the value of x.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio** of **Expenditure** (New : Initial) = 15 : 16

**Price** increase of 25% → **Ratio** of **Price** (New : Initial) = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4

**Consumption Ratio** = (Expenditure Ratio) ÷ (Price Ratio) = (15/5) : (16/4) = 3 : 4

**Decrease** in **Consumption** = (4 − 3) ÷ 4 × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32efc45ce71f4a435c01338a6383552ec8e9177b7d6ec1bd2ab1c2a159795f92.png] 

**Given:**

Initial **Expenditure** (E₁) = 16 | New **Expenditure** (E₂) = 15

Initial **Price** (P₁) = 100 | New **Price** (P₂) = 125 (due to 25% increase)

**Formula Used:**

**Expenditure** = **Price** × **Consumption**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial **Consumption** (C₁) = E₁ ÷ P₁ = 16 ÷ 100 = 0.16

⇒ New **Consumption** (C₂) = E₂ ÷ P₂ = 15 ÷ 125 = 0.12

⇒ Percentage **Decrease** in **Consumption** (x) = [(C₁ − C₂) ÷ C₁] × 100

⇒ x = [(0.16 − 0.12) ÷ 0.16] × 100

⇒ x = (0.04 ÷ 0.16) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Expenditure Rule

If **Expenditure** remains **constant**, the **Price** is inversely proportional to **Consumption**. If price increases by r%, consumption must decrease by [r/(100+r)] × 100%.

Successive Percentage Change

Total % change in **Expenditure** = a + b + (a × b)/100, where a is % change in **Price** and b is % change in **Consumption**.

Base Change Property

When calculating **percentage decrease**, always use the **original** (initial) value as the denominator in the base.</p

questions.question: A solid sphere of radius 7 cm is cut into two equal half, Find the increase in surface area of the object.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **solid sphere** is cut into two equal halves, two new **circular cross-sections** are created.

Each new face has an area of πr².

Increase in **Surface Area** = 2 × πr²

⇒ Increase = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ Increase = 44 × 7 = 308 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 308 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the **solid sphere** (r) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of Sphere = 4πr²

Total Surface Area of **Hemisphere** = 3πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/95ab81cbadfca7ee6b82c8fd8d36f19fc6bca78b3358c96e0920197fcff3000f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Surface Area of original sphere = 4 × π × (7)²

⇒ Total Surface Area of two hemispheres = 2 × (3 × π × (7)²) = 6 × π × (7)²

⇒ Increase in surface area = 6πr² − 4πr² = 2πr²

⇒ Increase = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ Increase = 2 × 22 × 7

⇒ Increase = 308 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 308 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Sphere

The volume of a solid sphere is given by the formula V = (4/3)πr³.

Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The area of the curved part only (excluding the base) is 2πr².

Total Surface Area of Hemisphere

The sum of the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr².</p

questions.question: After giving 20% discount, a shopkeeper still manages to earn 14(2)/(7)% profit. If the marked price of the article is Rs. 1000, then find the cost price of the article.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Marked Price (MP)** is given by (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%).

CP : MP = (100 − 20) : (100 + 14 2/7) = 80 : 114 2/7 = 80 : 800/7.

CP : MP = 7 : 10.

Given **Marked Price** = 10 units = Rs. 1000 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 100.

**Cost Price** = 7 units = 7 × 100 = Rs. 700.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:****Marked Price (MP)** = Rs. 1000, **Discount** = 20%, **Profit** = 14 2/7%.

**Formula:****Selling Price (SP)** = **MP** × (100 − D%)/100 and **CP** = **SP** × 100/(100 + P%).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/012e9b238d3146d78dda6ea531b839669f66c77bd9df86eca7d8a0cfaa8adf5b.png] 
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 1000 − (20% of 1000)

⇒ **SP** = 1000 − 200 = Rs. 800

⇒ **Profit %** = 14 2/7% = 100/7 % = 1/7 (in fraction)

⇒ **SP** = **CP** × (1 + Profit Fraction) = **CP** × (1 + 1/7) = **CP** × 8/7

⇒ 800 = **CP** × 8/7

⇒ **CP** = (800 × 7) / 8 = 100 × 7 = Rs. 700

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP-MP Relation Formula

The direct relation between **Cost Price** and **Marked Price** is CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Mark-up Percentage

**Mark-up %** = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100. It is the percentage by which the **Marked Price** is higher than the **Cost Price**.

Profit and Loss on CP

Always remember that **Profit** or **Loss** percentage is calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise in the question.</p

questions.question: If the sum of two numbers is 11 and the sum of their squares is 65, then the sum of their cubes will be:

Identify two numbers whose **sum** is 11: (1,10), (2,9), (3,8), (4,7), (5,6).

Check the **sum of squares**: 7² + 4² = 49 + 16 = 65. (Matches given condition).

Calculate **sum of cubes**: 7³ + 4³ = 343 + 64 = 407.

**∴ The correct answer is 407.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of numbers (x + y) = 11, Sum of squares (x² + y²) = 65.

**Formula Used:** (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy and x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² + y² − xy)

⇒ 11² = 65 + 2xy

⇒ 121 − 65 = 2xy

⇒ 56 = 2xy

⇒ xy = 28

⇒ x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² + y² − xy)

⇒ x³ + y³ = 11 × (65 − 28)

⇒ x³ + y³ = 11 × 37 = 407

**∴ The correct answer is 407.**

Difference of Cubes

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

questions.question: For a right-angled triangle, the perpendicular length is 2 cm more than the base and the hypotenuse is 4 cm more than the base of the right-angled triangle. Find the hypotenuse length of the triangle. (in cm)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use **Pythagorean Triplets** logic to identify values where the differences match (2 and 4).

The standard triplet (3, 4, 5) scaled by 2 gives **(6, 8, 10)**.

Checking the conditions: 8 − 6 = 2 cm (Perpendicular − Base) and 10 − 6 = 4 cm (Hypotenuse − Base).

The conditions are satisfied, so the hypotenuse is 10 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base of the triangle = b cm

Perpendicular (Height) = (b + 2) cm

Hypotenuse = (b + 4) cm

**Formula Used:**

**Pythagoras Theorem:** (Perpendicular)² + (Base)² = (Hypotenuse)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3153a408649ac987e1a396398033e5c095780a5467b15ffd7bc4c36468c5cdd9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (b + 2)² + b² = (b + 4)²

⇒ (b² + 4b + 4) + b² = b² + 8b + 16

⇒ 2b² + 4b + 4 = b² + 8b + 16

⇒ b² − 4b − 12 = 0

⇒ b² − 6b + 2b − 12 = 0

⇒ b(b − 6) + 2(b − 6) = 0

⇒ (b − 6)(b + 2) = 0

⇒ b = 6 or b = −2 (Length cannot be negative, so b = 6)

⇒ Hypotenuse = b + 4 = 6 + 4 = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common integer sets satisfying a² + b² = c² include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Area of Right-Angled Triangle

The area is calculated as Area = 1/2 × Base × Perpendicular. For this triangle, Area = 1/2 × 6 × 8 = 24 cm².

Circumradius of Right Triangle

The radius of the circumcircle is exactly half the length of the hypotenuse: R = Hypotenuse ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.</p

questions.question: A 3.5-billion-year-old Martian crater was recently named after which pioneering Indian geologist under the IAU’s planetary naming guidelines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M.S. Krishnan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• A 3.5 billion-year-old crater on Mars has been officially named after pioneering Indian geologist **M.S. Krishnan**, along with several Kerala-based names approved by the IAU for nearby smaller landforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The IAU has named a major Martian crater after **M.S. Krishnan**, recognising his foundational contributions to geological and planetary sciences.
 
• IAU rules allow large craters on Mars to be named after **deceased scientists** who have significantly advanced planetary research.
 
• The naming reflects international acknowledgement of India’s scientific heritage and Krishnan’s importance in Earth and planetary geology.
 
• This is part of IAU’s systematic planetary naming process, in place since **1919**, to ensure scientific consistency across planetary bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Kerala Names Accepted by IAU**__

 __
 
• Smaller craters and a vallis near the Krishnan crater have been named **Valiamala, Thumba, Bekal, Varkala** and **Periyar**.
 
• These reflect India’s cultural and historical significance on Martian maps.
 
 
 
• **IAU Planetary Naming Rules**__
 __
 
• Large craters: named after **deceased scientists** who made major contributions to planetary science.
 
• Small craters: named after **towns/villages** with populations under 1,00,000, and names must be easy to pronounce and culturally relevant.
 
• Planetary nomenclature provides an official registry of names for **planets, moons and ring systems**.
 
 
 
• **About M.S. Krishnan**__
 __
 
• A pioneering Indian geologist noted for shaping modern geological research in India.
 
• His contributions laid early foundations for structural geology and Earth sciences.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Planetary Nomenclature**__
 
 
• Ensures uniform naming standards across global scientific communities.
 
• Helps map Martian terrain for research, exploration and mission planning.
 
• Strengthens India’s representation in international planetary science.

questions.question: Which Indian state has issued a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to test farm equipment for women farmers to ensure ergonomic design and reduce drudgery?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **Government of Odisha** has introduced a **Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** for testing agricultural machinery and equipment specifically designed for **women farmers**.
 
• The SOP was finalised on **November 4, 2025** during an expert committee meeting.
 
• This initiative aims to ensure that **farm equipment is ergonomically suited to women’s body dimensions, posture, and strength**.
 
• The policy will help reduce **drudgery, musculoskeletal disorders, and other health impacts** commonly faced by women farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The SOP was developed after a **pilot study under the Shree Anna Abhiyan (formerly Odisha Millets Mission)** in five districts — **Sundargarh, Keonjhar, Koraput, Nuapada, and Gajapati**.
 
• The study tested farm equipment like **weeders, threshers, and sprayers** with direct participation from women farmers.
 
• The SOP integrates research from the **All India Coordinated Research Project on Ergonomics and Safety** and inputs from **Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT)** and **ICAR**.
 
• The **Department of Agriculture and Farmers Empowerment, Government of Odisha** is the nodal agency for implementing and scaling up the testing process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Need for the SOP**__

 __
 
• Farm tools and machinery are typically designed for men, ignoring women’s ergonomic needs.
 
• According to **ICAR**, over **50% of women farmers** suffer from severe musculoskeletal disorders due to ill-fitted tools.
 
• Common issues include **back pain (56.7%)**, **shoulder pain (59.4%)**, and **leg/foot pain (69.4%)**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Initiative**__
 __
 
• Ensures that farm equipment is **women-friendly and ergonomically safe**.
 
• Improves **productivity, comfort, and health outcomes** for women farmers.
 
• Supports the broader goal of **feminisation of agriculture** in India — where women now account for **64.4% of the agricultural workforce (2023–24)**, up from 57% in 2017–18.
 
 
 
• **Collaborating Institutions**__
 
 
• **Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT)**
 
• **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)**
 
• **All India Coordinated Research Project on Ergonomics and Safety**
